title: SDK Warmstart: Pocket Plan & 15-min Integrated Lab
content: Goal: compress the first-success path for an integrator down to 15 minutes (warmstart). This pocket plan is intentionally minimal: a single-page lab + 6 step checklist + smoke probes + fallback patterns. Meant for: SDK advocates, field engineers, on-call demoers, and quickstart docs.
content_3: - Observed pain: users spend 30–90 minutes wrestling with API keys, runtime errors, or network proxies before they hit a meaningful prompt. We want a frictionless demo for non-expert integrators (PMs, FE devs).
content_5:
- single-sample app (no infra beyond Docker or node)
- guided, copy-paste commands only (no Terraform)
- minimal config surface: API key + model name + endpoint
- immediate telemetry feedback (did their first request succeed?)
- clear rollback/failure recovery (what to try if blocked)
content_7:
1) Prep (2 min)
- Create account / use demo token: `REDWOOD_DEMO_TOKEN` (advocate supplies ephemeral token for workshop).
- Open repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples (branch: warmstart-pocket).
- Files to edit: `.env.example` -> `.env` (only REDWOOD_API_KEY).
content_8:
2) Run (4 min)
- Docker quick run: `docker run --rm -e REDWOOD_API_KEY=$REDWOOD_API_KEY ghcr.io/redwood-inference/warmstart-node:latest`
- Node quick run: `npm i && REDWOOD_API_KEY=$REDWOOD_API_KEY node samples/mini-chat.js`
- Expected output: streaming tokens, `response.complete: true`, sample score line. If no output in 10s, see smoke probes below.
content_9:
3) Inspect (3 min)
- Console shows: request id, latency (ms), tokens-in/tokens-out.
- Open dashboard snippet: /console/samples/<request-id> (example link printed by sample app).
- Check telemetry probe keys: `sdk.warmstart.first_request`, `sdk.warmstart.latency_ms`.
content_10:
4) Tweak prompt and model (3 min)
- Swap model: set `MODEL=redwood-alpha-compact` in `.env` and rerun. Observe latency and quality change.
- Try a short prompt change and compare token usage. Quick note: show `--dry-run` to estimate token cost without calling the API.
content_11:
5) Failure recovery (2 min)
- Most common failures and fixes:
  - 401 / invalid key: ensure `.env` exported, paste raw token, avoid trailing spaces.
  - 502 / gateway timeout: retry once with `REDWOOD_RETRY=1` and shorter sequence length.
  - TLS / proxy errors (corp networks): `export NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0` while debugging or use curl from a public network.
- If blocked, copy `request-id` from app and ping #sdk-warmstart slack with tag + request-id.
content_12:
6) Next steps (optional wins, 1–2 min)
- Enable `SDK_TELEMETRY=true` to get first-request dashboards.
- Run sample embedding: `node samples/embed-quick.js` and show vector dimension and size.
- Save sample as gist and link to onboarding ticket.
content_13: Smoke probes (automated checks run by sample app and CI):
content_14:
- probe/success: status==200 and streaming started within 2s
- probe/latency: p95 < 1200ms for compact models
- probe/telemetry: event sdk.warmstart.first_request emitted within 5s
- probe/cost-preview: dry-run token_estimate < 50 tokens for default prompt
content_17:
Sample CLI outputs (what to expect)
---
Request: r_3b8f4e
Model: redwood-alpha-compact
Latency: 920ms
Tokens in: 18
Tokens out: 46
Streaming: started
Telemetry: sdk.warmstart.first_request=1
---
content_18:
Minimal sample code (snippet to include in lab page)
- node: samples/mini-chat.js includes: 1) set REDWOOD_API_KEY 2) call /v1/chat with messages 3) stream stdout 4) print request-id and perf summary
- shell: curl example included with `-H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY'` and minimal JSON payload.
content_19:
Acceptance criteria for warmstart flow (for docs to be merged):
- 90% of new users in cohort A reach a streaming response within 15 minutes in local check run.
- sample app CI passes smoke probes on latest runtime.
- Readme < 300 words and contains 3 copy-paste commands only.
content_20:
UX copy quick sketches (tone: pragmatic, helpful):
- Title: "Warmstart SDK lab — 15 minutes to first response"
- Short lead: "Copy, paste, run. If it breaks, one command to collect diagnostics and notify support."
- Help blurbs: small inline callouts for 401, 502, and corporate proxy issues.
content_21:
Operational notes for advocates:
- Advocates should generate ephemeral tokens with 1-hour TTL for workshops (script in GH Actions).
- Have a fallback public demo server (read-only) that returns canned streaming output if user's network blocks outbound traffic.
- Roll a small monitoring dashboard (shared) with `sdk.warmstart.*` charts for demo sessions.
content_22:
Open questions / TODOs:
- Should warmstart use a dedicated demo model (quantized) to guarantee p95 < 1s? Tradeoff: quality vs predictability. (P0 decision for next week)
- Legal / security: can we distribute ephemeral tokens broadly for public meetups? Need legal OK.
- Should the sample app auto-attach console link for request replay? UX + privacy tradeoffs.
- Add short video GIF to README? -> yes, but create 30s recording in staging.
content_23:
Feedback log (notes from initial alpha run):
- Nov workshop: devs liked copy-paste Docker path best; corporate devs hit proxy issue more often; add single-line curl proxy hint.
- Alpha participants requested a 'cost estimate' line pre-call. Implemented dry-run in samples/estimate.js.
content_24:
Quick checklist (to ship a warmstart-ready advertorial):
- [ ] README < 300 words with 3 commands
- [ ] Docker image published + tag `warmstart-latest`
- [ ] GH Actions workflow to generate ephemeral tokens for advocates
- [ ] Smoke probes in sample CI (pass p95 latency)
- [ ] One-pager PDF for sales with common error fixes
- [ ] Slack #sdk-warmstart alias + runbook link
